questions.stem: A 22-year-old woman requested HPV vaccination. She reported sex with both men and women with five sex partners in the last year. She was tested annually for STIs and HIV . She tested positive for chlamydia 2 years ago and was treated with azithromycin 1 g. All STI tests were negative at her last screening 6 months ago.
questions.lead_in: What is the most appropriate action?

options.text: Do not vaccinate. Explain that she has likely already been exposed to HPV , and vaccination is not indicated
Do not vaccinate. She is too old to receive the vaccine
Test for presence of HPV using a vaginal swab. If HPV is present, do not vaccinate

questions.explanation: Vaccinate with three-dose series HPV vaccination is recommended for adolescents age 11 or 12 years. Vaccination is also recommended for females between the ages of 13 and 26 and for males between the ages of 13 through 21 who were not adequately vaccinated previously. HPV vaccination is also recommended for gay, bisexual, and other men who have sex with men, transgender people, and those with some immunocompromising conditions between ages 22 and 26 years, if inadequately vaccinated in the past. The vaccine should be administered regardless of history of exposure.
questions.source: Comprehensive Review of ID · Quiz 3 Q24

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman attended care to discuss immunizations. She had recently been diagnosed with HIV and had started ART 2 weeks previously. She denied a history of chickenpox or measles as a child. She reported 10 lifetime sexual partners. Investigations: CD4 count 115 cells/mm3 HIV-1 RNA viral load 145,000 copies/mL Hepatitis B surface Ag negative Hepatitis B surface Ab negative Hepatitis B core Ab positive Hepatitis B DNA <20 IU/mL VZV IgG negative Measles IgG negative
questions.lead_in: In addition to seasonal influenza vaccination, what immunizations should be offered?
questions.explanation: Hepatitis B virus vaccine The patient has isolated hepatitis B virus (HBV) core antibody positivity but no evidence of chronic HBV or immunity to HBV based on negative HBV DNA and HBV surface antibody. Therefore HBV vaccination is indicated at this time even though the response rate may be lower given the low CD4 count. The patient’s CD4 count <200 cells/mm3 is a contraindication to live attenuated vaccines including herpes zoster (shingles), varicella (chickenpox), and measles, mumps, rubella (MMR) vaccines. HPV vaccine is indicated for women through the age of 26 based on the licensing studies and since sexually active patients above this age are more likely to already have acquired HPV infection.
questions.source: Comprehensive Review of ID · Quiz 3 Q37

questions.stem: A 35-year-old man was reviewed prior to treatment with eculizumab, a complement inhibitor. He was known to have paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria and had failed treatment with plasma exchanges.
questions.lead_in: What is the most important immunization to arrange before treatment?
questions.explanation: Meningococcal ACWY and menB There is a boxed warning on the eculizumab due to meningococcal infections which may be fatal or life-threatening. Eculizumab recipients are 1000–2000× increased risk of meningococcal infections compared to healthy individuals. Therefore there is a strong recommendation to vaccinate against meningococcus at least 2 weeks prior to the initiation of eculizumab. If they cannot be vaccinated 2 weeks prior, they should receive antibiotic prophylaxis until 2 weeks after vaccination. Patients are also at risk for infections due to other encapsulated organisms, and the patients are likely to have chronic renal failure, so other vaccinations that should be considered are influenza, Hib, and pneumococcal vaccines, but meningococcal vaccine is imperative.
questions.source: Comprehensive Review of ID · Quiz 3 Q39

questions.stem: A 23-year-old healthcare worker who was 12 weeks pregnant sought advice on the vaccinations she required before starting work.

options.text: Combined tetanus, diphtheria, acellular pertussis, and inactivated polio vaccine (DTap/IPV)

questions.explanation: Varicella-zoster vaccine Live-attenuated virus vaccines, such as VAR vaccine, are contraindicated in pregnancy. Influenza and pertussis containing vaccines such as DTap/IPV are indicated in pregnancy. Hepatitis A and hepatitis B vaccines may be safely administered if indicated in pregnancy.
questions.source: Comprehensive Review of ID · Quiz 4 Q44

questions.question: A 22 year old man with IBD has stopped prednisone 2 weeks ago and is about to start INFLIXIMAB in 4 weeks. He was born in canada. As listed below he has received his childhood vaccinations, but no other vaccines. Vaccine record: Received 3 doses of DTap-IPV-HIb, 1 dose of MMR (12mos), 1 dose of Men C, 1 dose of Pneuc-7

parts.text: List 4 tests you would do to screen infections before starting infliximab
What vaccine(s) would you provide for this patient to improve his protection against pneumococcal disease. If applicable, what is the timeline of administration?
Other than DTap List 6 other vaccines that should be provided for this patient
In relation to infliximab start when should inactivated vaccines be given? And why?
In relation to infliximab start when should live vaccines be given? And why?

cohort_answer.text: Tests: Everyone - LTBI, hep B & hep C, HIV; also dimorphics, TB, strongyloides, HTLV, HSV, VZV. Pneumococcal vaccine: PCV-13 followed by PPV-23 8 weeks later. Other vaccines: 2 other doses of MMR, influenza vaccine, hepatitis B, PCV-13, PPV-23, Hib, HPV, HAV, herpes zoster vaccine. Inactivated vaccines: prior to initiation at least 2 weeks and preferably 3-4 weeks; during, 2 weeks at time of minimal immunosuppression; following discontinuation, wait more than 3 months. Live vaccines: prior to initiation at least 4-6 weeks; after discontinuation, 3 months.

questions.question: Name 2 vaccines that indicated in a HEALTHY PREGNANT female.

parts.text: Name 2 vaccines that indicated in a HEALTHY PREGNANT female.

questions.model_answer: 2 vaccines indicated in a healthy pregnant woman: (1) inactivated influenza vaccine (any trimester); (2) Tdap (tetanus-diphtheria-acellular pertussis) vaccine, typically given between 27-32 weeks gestation each pregnancy to provide passive pertussis protection to the newborn.
questions.beyond_mandell: Canadian Immunization Guide/ACIP recommendations for immunization in pregnancy; RSV vaccine (e.g., Abrysvo) is now also recommended in pregnancy per updated 2023-2024 guidance, an option not reflected in the original Mandell chapter listing.
